title: Understand What The Client Actually Needs
summary: Before anyone touches code, sit down directly with the client to define real problems, user roles, and MVP features.
whyItMatters: If you skip this and start coding based on assumptions, you'll build the wrong system beautifully. No amount of clean code fixes a product that solves the wrong problem.

tasks.text: Interview the client about the exact problem they are trying to solve and current workarounds (paper forms, Excel, walk-ins, etc.)
Identify who will actually use the system and define clear user roles (e.g., Admin, Staff, Citizen, Client)
Separate 'Must-Have for Launch' (MVP) from 'Nice-to-Have Later' feature requests

formFields.label: MVP Features for Launch
formFields.placeholder: e.g. User Login, Submit Form, Dashboard

title: Sketch The Pages Before Designing Them
summary: Roughly draw visual page layouts on paper, a whiteboard, or Figma before choosing colors, typography, and styling.
whyItMatters: It is much cheaper to erase a box on paper than to rewrite a finished UI component. Catching missing elements like search bars early saves hours of rework.

tasks.text: Sketch a rough layout for every major screen or page
Present rough wireframes to the client and obtain explicit sign-off before making design decisions

title: Set Up How The Team Will Work Together
summary: Establish clear developer roles, Git branching strategies, and shared task management boards.
whyItMatters: Even with AI writing code quickly, someone must organize task allocation. Without clear git flow & roles, you will suffer merge conflicts and duplicated work.

tasks.text: Assign clear roles: who handles frontend, backend, database, testing, and QA
Agree on a simple Git branching setup (e.g., main=stable, dev=staging, feature/task-name=dev)
Set up a shared project board (Trello, Notion, or GitHub Projects) to track active and completed tasks

title: Set Up The Tools And Environment
summary: Standardize Node, PHP, or MySQL runtime versions across laptops and choose hosting early.
whyItMatters: Choosing hosting late can force code refactoring if host limits runtime versions or storage. Standardizing environments prevents 'works on my machine' bugs.

tasks.text: Agree on exact runtime versions (Node.js, PHP, MySQL/PostgreSQL) across the whole team
Document step-by-step setup instructions for fresh clones in docs/README.md
Decide hosting platform early (Railway, Vercel, VPS, Hostinger, Shared Hosting) to verify limits

title: Fill Out The Context Docs (The AI Briefing Kit)
summary: Populate the 5 essential markdown files in context/ using verified project information from Steps 1–4.
whyItMatters: This is the essence of structured AI-assisted development. Giving AI full project context eliminates random guessing and inconsistent code generation.

tasks.text: Complete PRD.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, SCHEMA.md, DESIGN.md, and RULES.md using gathered data
Reference this context folder whenever prompting AI tools (Claude, Cursor, Antigravity)

formFields.label: Key Constraints/Deadlines
formFields.placeholder: e.g. Due in 4 weeks, Budget limits

title: Agree On Work Approval Process & Data Security
summary: Establish milestone review gates, client approval protocols, and security access controls.
whyItMatters: For systems handling sensitive citizen or corporate data, security and milestone sign-offs are mandatory requirements from day one.

tasks.text: Establish a clear review process for how and when the client approves each phase or feature
Plan data protection, Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), and privacy levels for sensitive records
